reported.title: Pump chatters at threshold due to missing hysteresis
reported.description: The control logic at lines 71-78 uses a single threshold START_CM (45.0) for both starting and stopping, so any level fluctuation around 45 cm flips the pump on and off with no deadband. Combined with the raw, unfiltered analogRead at line 22 and the 40 ms poll at line 63, sensor noise directly toggles D7, producing the measured 64 toggles in a 5000 ms window (limit 2) during threshold hover and 34 toggles during rapid oscillation. The spec requires stopping at 30.0 cm, which is never implemented, so no hysteresis band exists to suppress chatter. D7 toggled 64 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.32 s (limit 2), and 84 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D7 must not toggle more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window (No short cycling)

judge_input.spec:
- Linear water-level sensor on A1 at 10 mV/cm; sump pump contactor on D7; silence pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Start the pump when level reaches 45.0 cm or higher; stop the pump when level falls to 30.0 cm or lower.
- Holding D4 LOW latches silence mode and keeps the pump OFF until reset (power cycle).
- Pump output must not toggle more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Every 800 ms print `sump cm=<level> pump=<0|1> mute=<0|1>` with level to one decimal place.
- Apply pump start/stop within 500 ms of a sustained band crossing.
